rules.name: Core Courses
rules.desc: Except for course, all Core Courses must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a grade of B or higher. A grade of B- or lower triggers automatic review by the PhD Program Committee, which will determine the remediation plan and, in some cases, whether the student can continue in the PhD program.

rules.name: Methodologic Coursework (9 units)
rules.notes:
Any 200-level STATS course (other than STATS 260) will fulfill the requirement.
Note: If you are interested in another course, please check with the PhD program director or advisor to make sure that it is compatible with this requirement.

rules.name: Specializations and Electives (9 units, at least 3 different substantive content areas)
rules.desc:
Students must take electives from at least three substantive content areas for a minimum of 9 units. Below are examples of different areas and a longer list of electives. Students should check with the PhD program director and/or their advisor to determine if other classes are compatible with this requirement.

rules.name: Oral Examinations and Dissertation Draft
rules.desc:
Students begin working on their dissertation after passing the oral qualifying exam in Year 3. Upon completion students submit their thesis to the Registrar and graduate. PhD students in Epidemiology and Population Health tend to complete the program in 4 to 4.5 years (median 4.3 years).
The defense consists of two parts:
1. Public Seminar: The student will give a 30-minute talk open to faculty and students, followed by a 15-minute question and answer session.
2. Closed-Door Session: The closed session will be at least 90 minutes, during which the student will answer additional questions posed by the committee members.
rules.notes: See EPH Education Handbook for additional details.

rules.name: Dissertation Overview
rules.desc:
Dissertations can be any combination of substantive, methodologic, or theoretical topics as long as they fall under the student’s area of specialty or are linked by a common methodologic approach. There must be some substantive methodologic innovation in at least one part of the dissertation. Two formats are accepted: The candidate can prepare three papers for publication linked by an articulated theoretical perspective and substantive areas. Alternatively, the candidate can prepare a traditional dissertation (including sections on problem formulation, theory, hypotheses, methods, data analysis, findings, and study implications).
Substantive methodologic innovation is defined as: (1) developing a novel methodologic approach, (2) evaluating a novel methodology (e.g., through simulation studies), (3) using an existing methodology in a novel way, or (4) exploiting or linking large datasets in novel ways to answer epidemiologic or clinical questions.
The dissertation should contain the following elements, at a minimum, and must also meet University formatting requirements:
1. 1-page lay summary. Students will clearly articulate what they accomplished and why it is important.
2. 2-page introduction. Students will highlight their research's overall background, significance, and aims, as well as the connecting themes of their three projects.
3. Body of the thesis. Students will include three papers for publication, each of which will consist of an expanded methodology section. The expanded methodology section will contain more written detail than would typically be included in a published manuscript and additional tables and figures. Students opting for a traditional dissertation will consist of sections on problem formulation, theory, hypotheses, methods, data analysis, findings, and study implications.
4. Conclusion. Students will succinctly synthesize the meaning and impact of their findings while tying together disparate themes from the papers/chapters and presenting a vision for future research needs in the area—minimum of three pages.
Detailed guidelines for the preparation and submission of dissertations are published on the Registrar’s Office of Student Affairs: Dissertation and Thesis Submission.
